unit_label: CB Module E unit 4: financial stability (courseware unit 16)

facts.statement: Financial stability, the 2008 crisis and the institutional framework (courseware): the global financial crisis of 2008 arose from subprime mortgages, mortgage-backed securities and credit default swaps, and Lehman Brothers failed on 15 September 2008; the courseware cites definitions of financial stability by Mishkin, Reddy and Vasudevan; the Reserve Bank responded to the crisis with liquidity and rate measures; the Reserve Bank has a role in financial stability through regulation, supervision, payment systems and monetary policy; after the crisis the institutional framework changed, with the Financial Stability Oversight Council under the Dodd-Frank Act in the US, a new structure in the UK, the European Systemic Risk Board in the EU and the Financial Stability and Development Council (FSDC) in India; the courseware says price stability alone does not ensure financial stability.
facts.locator: S05 courseware unit 16, printed pp. 375-387 (PDF pp. 392-404), sections 16.1 to 16.3

facts.statement: Risks, early warning and liquidity (courseware): risks to financial stability include herd behaviour, payment system failures and asset price collapse; early warning signals are indicators of crises, including the Kaminsky-Lizondo-Reinhart (KLR) signals approach; the Reserve Bank publishes the Financial Stability Report; liquidity management in banks follows the 14 principles of the Basel Committee for sound liquidity risk management, including that the management structure to execute the liquidity strategy includes the ongoing involvement of members of senior management, and that when limits are set on liquid assets as a percentage of short-term liabilities there should be a discount to reflect price volatility.
facts.locator: S05 courseware unit 16, printed pp. 387-398 (PDF pp. 404-415), sections 16.3 to 16.5

facts.statement: Supervision and the Basel framework (courseware): the Board for Financial Supervision (BFS) was constituted in November 1994 as a Reserve Bank board committee, with the Governor as Chairman, the Deputy Governor and four Directors of the Central Board; CAMELS is the rating model for banks and CALCS for foreign banks; the OSMOS (off-site monitoring and surveillance) system started in 1995; the supervisory initiatives include risk based supervision, prompt corrective action (PCA), the Credit Information Bureau of India (CIBIL, 2000) and debt recovery tribunals; the Basel Committee originated after the Herstatt failure and was established in 1975; it issued the Core Principles for Effective Banking Supervision; the New Basel Accord rests on three pillars: minimum capital requirements, the supervisory review process and market discipline.
facts.locator: S05 courseware unit 16, printed pp. 398-408 (PDF pp. 415-425), sections 16.5 to 16.7

facts.statement: Basel II and Basel III in India (courseware): the Reserve Bank adopted a gradual consultative approach; Basel II implementation started with a parallel run from April 1, 2006; banks were to adopt the standardised approach for credit risk, the basic indicator approach for operational risk and the standardised duration method for market risk; implementation was to be by March 31, 2007 but was postponed to March 31, 2008 for foreign banks and Indian banks with a presence outside India and to March 31, 2009 for all other scheduled commercial banks (except regional rural banks); banks were to reach a Tier 1 capital ratio of six per cent by March 31, 2010; Basel III capital regulation was implemented from April 1, 2013 in phases and the liquidity coverage ratio from January 1, 2015 with full implementation from January 1, 2019; the challenges named are capital, liquidity, technology, skill development and governance; the Basel III proposals raise the minimum common equity from 2 per cent to 4.5 per cent and Tier 1 from 4 per cent to 6 per cent, add a capital conservation buffer of 2.5 per cent so that total capital rises from 8 per cent to 10.5 per cent, add a leverage ratio, a countercyclical buffer, the LCR and the net stable funding ratio (NSFR); the BCBS dealt with systemically important financial institutions (SIFIs) through indicators, additional loss absorbency and enhanced supervision; the Financial Stability Board set principles for sound compensation practices, with deferral and claw-back of variable pay; the Banking Codes and Standards Board of India was set up in November 2003 on the UK model.
facts.locator: S05 courseware unit 16, printed pp. 408-415 (PDF pp. 425-432), sections 16.7 to 16.10

facts.statement: Liberalisation, markets and standards (courseware): since 1998-99 the Reserve Bank adopted a multiple indicator approach for monetary policy; the fixed rate repo was introduced in December 1997 and the liquidity adjustment facility (LAF) from June 2000, with the repo rate as floor and the Bank Rate as ceiling of the informal corridor; the Financial Markets Committee (FMC) reviews liquidity and interest rate conditions daily and a Financial Markets Department (FMD) provides market surveillance; the infrastructure includes the Delivery versus Payment system, the Clearing Corporation of India, RTGS, CFMS and NDS; transparency helps market participants and the monetary policy transmission mechanism; the Special Data Dissemination Standards (SDDS) and General Data Dissemination Standards (GDDS) were devised by the IMF; the Financial Stability Forum was set up in 1999 and the G-20 was formed in 1999; the standard setters include the BCBS, the Committee on Payment and Settlement Systems (CPSS), the Financial Action Task Force (FATF, established at the G7 summit in Paris in 1989 with 40 recommendations to combat money laundering), the International Accounting Standards Committee (formed in 1973), the International Association of Insurance Supervisors (1994), IFAC, IMF, IOSCO, OECD and the World Bank; compliance with standards is reported in the Reports on the Observance of Standards and Codes (ROSCs).
facts.locator: S05 courseware unit 16, printed pp. 415-430 (PDF pp. 432-447), sections 16.11 to 16.17

payload.title: Financial stability, the 2008 crisis and the post-crisis framework
payload.core_explanation_md:
**Cause:** the 2008 crisis grew from **subprime mortgages, mortgage-backed securities and credit default swaps**; **Lehman Brothers** failed on **15 September 2008**.

**Lesson:** **price stability alone does not ensure financial stability**, so central banks added financial stability as an objective with **regulation, supervision, payment systems and monetary policy**.

**New bodies:** **FSOC** (US, Dodd-Frank), the **ESRB** (EU) and the **FSDC** (India).
payload.expanded_explanation_md: The unit treats financial stability as a state in which institutions, markets and infrastructure keep working through shocks. The RBI responded to the crisis with liquidity and rate measures. The post-crisis institutional change moved supervisors toward macro-prudential oversight.

self_check.prompt_text: Why is price stability not enough for financial stability?
self_check.expected_takeaway: Severe financial instability can arise even when prices are stable, as the 2008 crisis showed.

payload.title: Risks, early warning signals and liquidity principles
payload.core_explanation_md:
**Risks:** **herd behaviour**, **payment system failure** and **asset price collapse**.

**Early warning:** indicators of impending crisis, such as the **KLR signals approach**; the RBI publishes the **Financial Stability Report**.

**Liquidity:** the **14 Basel principles** require **senior management involvement** in executing the liquidity strategy; limits on liquid assets against short-term liabilities need a **discount for price volatility**.
payload.expanded_explanation_md: Early warning indicators are a macro-prudential tool: they flag vulnerabilities before a crisis occurs. Liquidity principles apply to every bank regardless of size.

self_check.prompt_text: Who must be involved in executing the liquidity strategy under the Basel principles?
self_check.expected_takeaway: Members of senior management, on an ongoing basis.

payload.title: Supervision machinery and the Basel framework
payload.core_explanation_md:
**BFS (November 1994):** Governor as Chairman, Deputy Governor and **four** Directors of the Central Board.

**Ratings:** **CAMELS** for banks, **CALCS** for foreign banks; **OSMOS** started in **1995**.

**Tools:** risk based supervision, **PCA**, **CIBIL (2000)**, DRTs.

**Basel:** the committee began after the Herstatt failure; **three pillars**: minimum capital, supervisory review, market discipline.
payload.expanded_explanation_md: The BFS gives supervision a dedicated board separate from monetary policy. Off-site monitoring complements on-site inspection by using returns filed by banks.

self_check.prompt_text: Name the three pillars of the New Basel Accord.
self_check.expected_takeaway: Minimum capital requirements, supervisory review and market discipline.

payload.title: Basel II and III implementation in India
payload.core_explanation_md:
**Basel II:** parallel run from **1 April 2006**; **standardised approach** (credit), **basic indicator** (operational), **standardised duration** (market); foreign banks and those with overseas presence by **31 March 2008** and others by **31 March 2009**; **Tier 1 six per cent** by 31 March 2010.

**Basel III:** from **1 April 2013**; **common equity 2% → 4.5%**, **Tier 1 4% → 6%**, **2.5% conservation buffer** takes total capital **8% → 10.5%**; adds leverage ratio, countercyclical buffer, **LCR** (from **1 January 2015**) and **NSFR**.
payload.expanded_explanation_md: The five challenges named are capital, liquidity, technology, skill development and governance. For SIFIs the BCBS planned indicators, extra loss absorbency and enhanced supervision; the FSB set compensation principles with deferral and claw-back.

self_check.prompt_text: By how much does the capital conservation buffer lift total capital?
self_check.expected_takeaway: 2.5 percentage points, from 8 to 10.5 per cent.

payload.title: Liberalisation, transparency, and international standards
payload.core_explanation_md:
**Monetary policy:** the **multiple indicator approach** from **1998-99**; **fixed rate repo** (December 1997) and **LAF** (June 2000), with repo as floor and Bank Rate as ceiling.

**Market infrastructure:** DvP, CCIL, RTGS, CFMS, NDS; **FMC** reviews conditions daily; **FMD** conducts surveillance.

**Standards:** **SDDS/GDDS** (IMF), **FSF/G-20 (1999)**, **FATF (1989)** with **40 recommendations**, **ROSCs** report compliance.
payload.expanded_explanation_md: Transparency helps markets form expectations and strengthens policy transmission. Standards are only as effective as the compliance behind them, which the ROSCs assess.

unresolved: The unit is the courseware account of financial stability. No primary source (Basel Committee texts, RBI circulars, Financial Stability Reports) was retrieved; implementation dates and ratios are taught only as the courseware states them and may have changed by the 30 June 2026 cut-off.

Held back as dated and not asked in any question: the CRAR, provision coverage and other figures from the Financial Stability Report of December 2021, and the CRR and SLR levels quoted for 2011 to 2017.

The courseware check-your-progress key gives answer (d) for the question on the G-20 formation (US, UK and France) although the unit text says the G-20 was formed in 1999 on the initiative of the US Government; and answer (a) BIS for the code of good practices on transparency in monetary and financial policies; both conflict with or are not supported by the text, so neither is taught or asked.

The courseware gives the leverage ratio as monitored at 4.5 per cent in one place and the BCBS leverage proposal elsewhere; no leverage figure is asked. Basel III capital start (April 1, 2013), LCR start (1 January 2015) and full LCR (1 January 2019) are taught as stated.
The unit says 25 core principles in one place without listing them; the number is taught as stated and flagged as dated.
Numbers in the numerical items are invented or simple arithmetic and checked in tests/content/batch-cb-e-u04-b001.test.ts.
